title: Virtual, Non-virtual, Sliced
explanation:
`p->name()`: `name` is virtual, so the call is dispatched on the *dynamic* type of the object (a `Dog`) through its vtable, giving `Dog`.

`p->kind()`: `kind` is not virtual, so the compiler picks it from the *static* type of the pointer (`Animal*`), giving `animal`. `Dog::kind` hides it but doesn't override it.

`show(d)` takes an `Animal` **by value**. Only the `Animal` part of `d` is copied into the parameter; this is called *object slicing*. The copy really is an `Animal` (with `Animal`'s vtable), so even the virtual call gives `Animal`. Pass polymorphic objects by reference or pointer.
try_this: Change `show` to take `const Animal&`. What does it print now, and why?
